finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[RT-1] Unauthenticated/token endpoint allows abuse
File: src/pages/api/connection_details.ts (L1-L160)
Evidence: The POST handler issues LiveKit AccessTokens and returns ws_url without any authentication, rate limit, CAPTCHAs, or abuse checks and also exposes an "is_universe_guest" bypass that creates tokens without validating caller identity. This directly mints credentials that let clients connect to LiveKit and publish/subscribe/data-publish.
Impact: An attacker can spam token creation and/or spawn many clients, exhausting LiveKit API quotas, client connection capacity, or incurring cost — causing connection failures and dropped service for legitimate users.
Fix: Require authenticated requests (or short-lived exchange tokens), add per-IP/user rate limits and quotas, validate/limit guest issuance, and throttle token creation (CAPTCHA, recaptcha, or proof-of-work) before minting tokens.

[RT-2] Synchronous pre-checks call LiveKit for identity uniqueness (racy / rate-limited)
File: src/pages/api/connection_details.ts (L1-L160)
Evidence: Before issuing a token the handler calls roomService.getParticipant(room, username) to enforce uniqueness; that is an external REST call on every join attempt and is used as a pre-check rather than an atomic operation.
Impact: Under concurrent join attempts this creates a race (two clients can pass the check concurrently) and at scale the synchronous REST calls will hit LiveKit rate limits and latency, causing failed joins or blocking token issuance.
Fix: Remove the fragile pre-check and rely on atomic server-side enforcement (or LiveKit connection rejection) or implement a fast server-side lock/lease (DB/Redis) or a single-authority allocator plus retry/backoff to avoid racing and reduce REST call volume.

[RT-3] Uncached listParticipants call for room counts (polling / API overload)
File: src/pages/api/room_info/[room].ts (L1-L120)
Evidence: The GET handler directly calls roomService.listParticipants(room) on each request and returns participants.length, with no caching, rate-limiting, or aggregation.
Impact: High-frequency polling or many clients concurrently requesting room counts will fan out to LiveKit REST API and can exhaust API rate limits or increase latency, causing degraded UX and token/join failures elsewhere.
Fix: Cache participant counts (short TTL), add endpoint rate limits, and/or push room participant updates via webhooks/notifications into a shared cache (Redis) instead of querying LiveKit on every request.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[RT-4] Guest bypass enables anonymous mass-joins
File: src/pages/api/connection_details.ts (L1-L160)
Evidence: The is_universe_guest flag bypasses the normal participant-existence check and mints tokens with metadata is_universe_guest:true without verifying the caller.
Impact: This enables unauthenticated clients to obtain tokens and join rooms en masse, increasing risk of resource exhaustion and impersonation.
Fix: Require a server-side attestation for guest issuance (signed invite token, rate-limited guest registry, or limited-scope tokens with strict quotas).

--- INFO ---

[RT-5] LiveKit transports handled by external service (no local WebSocket server)
File: package.json / src/pages/api/*
Evidence: The app uses livekit-server-sdk to mint tokens and query rooms; there is no in-process websocket server code (no socket.io/ws routes).
